summary.value: Foliar lesions appear yellow, grey, or bluish; single or groups of yellow spots appear on older leaves, often growing together to form light brown necrotic areas, with leaves becoming puckered and distorted. Dense gray-blue sporulation appears on the undersides of leaf lesions.
summary.quote: Foliar lesions appear yellow, grey, or bluish characteristic of blue mold.

value: Keep the growing area as thoroughly drained as possible
Maintain appropriate plant spacing and nutrition to prevent excess growth and humidity in the canopy
Apply fungicides when the pathogen is most vulnerable

treatments.quote: one of the best strategies to prevent the development of an epidemic is to keep the growing area as thoroughly drained as possible. pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Rhizoctonia solani is a soil-borne plant pathogenic fungus in the phylum Basidiomycota

type_of_disease.quote: Rhizoctonia solani is a soil-borne plant pathogenic fungus in the phylum Basidiomycota

value: Foliar
Stem
affected_parts.quote: lower leaves turn brown and the presence of brown web-like mycelium may be observed attached to leaves and stems

summary.value: Symptoms on leaves begin as small, round, water-soaked spots about 2 to 3 mm in diameter that expand into large circular spots of concentric rings with a characteristic 'bullseye' appearance; tissue in the center may drop out giving a shot-hole appearance.
summary.quote: Symptoms on leaves develop around 48 hours after infection and begin as small, round, water-soaked spots about 2 to 3 mm in diameter (Figure 3).

diagnostic_features.value: Expanded lesions first become light green, almost transparent, with irregular margins and then form large circular spots of concentric rings, taking on a characteristic 'bullseye' appearance; tissue in the center of the lesions is thin and may drop out, giving a shot-hole appearance to the leaf.
diagnostic_features.quote: Expanded lesions first become light green, almost transparent, with irregular margins and then form large circular spots of concentric rings, taking on a characteristic 'bullseye' appearance (Figures 5-6). Tissue in the center of the lesions is thin and may drop out, giving a shot-hole appearance to the leaf (Figure 7).

value: Ventilation is critical
Plants with stem lesions should not be transplanted into the field
Sanitation and good growing practices are the best defense against target spot
Maintaining nitrogen within the recommended range of 75 to 125 ppm will help suppress, but not eliminate, this disease
Steam treatment for used pots and trays (center of stack held at 75 to 80Â°C for one hour)
Practices that open the plant canopy, increase air circulation, and reduce leaf wetness
Early harvesting of lower leaves from infected plants
Isolates of T. harzianum can reduce the growth of R. solani and enhance disease control
Fungicides containing Azoxystrobin and Mancozeb applied preventatively as a foliar spray
treatments.quote: Fungicides containing Azoxystrobin and Mancozeb have good activity against target spot. These products can be applied preventatively as a foliar spray for target spot.
